- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.6) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.4) or shows negative momentum — model fails to capture downward bias.
- Lagged corrections: if true outcome dips after a forecast spike, reduce next-period forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 2–5% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment swings — dampen forecast slope if sentiment volatility >0.3.
- Spike recovery: after a sharp price spike, forecast should taper off — don’t assume continuation; reduce forecast growth rate by 30–50% for 2–3 periods.
- Sentiment + price divergence: if sentiment >0.6 but price is flat or falling, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with sentiment.
- Avoid “sentiment-driven” overconfidence: if sentiment is high but recent price action is weak, don’t extrapolate — cap forecast growth at 3–5% unless confirmed trend.
